Senses.Explanation: Literally, to sever an arm. In the Chan record it overwhelmingly names the founding episode in which Shenguang, later named Huike, stands in the snow before Bodhidharma, cuts off his left arm, and places it before him. The lamp account has Bodhidharma say, 'you have now cut off your arm before me; your seeking may be accepted,' and then rename him Huike. Later records compress the episode into paired formulas—'standing in the snow and cutting off the arm,' 'cutting off the arm and pacifying the mind,' or 'face the wall for nine years / cut off the arm and pacify the mind'—and repeatedly reopen it as a public question. One master asks, 'what did the cutting off of the arm accomplish?' and strikes the staff before leaving the seat. Another is asked why one cuts off an arm to seek the Way if this house style is inherent in everyone; he replies, 'there are many mistaken understandings.' Still another says, 'why cut off an arm and seek elsewhere?' The Chan-specific bend is that Huike's bodily act becomes compact lineage and interview language, quoted, challenged, and criticized across later records. These later uses do not authorize this entry to declare the act a required sacrifice or explain its intention beyond what the accounts say.
Senses.Note: Zen-allowlist count: 563 hits in 216 texts. Family check covered standing in the snow (立雪), Shenguang or Huike (神光／慧可), pacifying the mind (安心), seeking the Way or teaching (求道／求法), nine years facing the wall (面壁九年), and the Second Patriarch (二祖). All refer back to the same bodily act; narrative, epithet, and later question are not different things. Names remain contextual because Huike is a lineage patriarch and belongs on the master roster, not as a separate dictionary figure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自斷左臂。置于祖前。祖知是法器。乃曰。諸佛最初求道。為法忘形。汝今斷臂吾前。求亦可在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Narrative core: Shenguang cuts off his left arm and places it before Bodhidharma; Bodhidharma acknowledges the act.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有神光法師，立雪斷臂，堅求諸佛要道，師為易名慧可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compact lineage formula: Shenguang stands in the snow, cuts off his arm, seeks the essential Way, and is renamed Huike.

Occurrences.Kwic: 少室巖前，祖師斷臂。且道斷臂作箇什麼？卓拄杖一下，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 續古尊宿語要, Ciming Chuyuan section. Ciming Chuyuan is the exact hall speaker: he invokes the patriarch cutting off his arm before Shaoshi Cliff, asks what the cutting accomplished, strikes once with the staff, and steps down.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「者段家風，人人本具，因甚斷臂求道？」師云：「錯會不少。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 空谷道澄禪師語錄. The exact actor is an unnamed monk: he asks 因甚斷臂求道. No personal name remains after the six-rung review.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一一真常獨露，何須斷臂別求？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 百愚禪師語錄. Baiyu Jingsi is the exact actor: his 弁山上堂 asks 何須斷臂別求.

Occurrences.Kwic: 二祖親傳曾斷臂，曾斷臂，血常流，直至而今痛未休。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Verse retrospect: 'the Second Patriarch personally received the transmission and once cut off his arm; the blood still flows, and to this day the pain has not ceased.'
